title: Dalal Street Braces for Record August Week with 11 Listings and Fresh IPO Pipeline
excerpt: After a blockbuster July headlined by Indo-MIM's 44% listing pop, India's primary market stays hot with ₹9,500 crore worth of new issues and nearly a dozen market debuts slated for early August.
body:
• Eleven companies, including healthcare giant Manipal Health and green energy player Juniper Green Energy, are set to make their stock market debuts between August 3 and August 7.
  • Fresh IPOs from Ardee Industries (₹426 crore mainboard), Anawil Wire & Engineering, Aegeus Technologies, and others will open for subscription in the first week of August.
  • Indo-MIM's blockbuster 44% listing gain and Poojaa Precision's 259x oversubscription signal robust investor appetite despite foreign investor pullback.
  • A ₹60,000 crore IPO pipeline looms for the coming months, with marquee names like InMobi, MakeMyTrip, and NSE preparing for public offerings.

India's primary market is heading into its busiest week of the year. After a record-setting July that saw billions of dollars flow into initial public offerings, at least 11 companies are preparing to list on the BSE and NSE in the first week of August, while a fresh batch of IPOs opens for investor subscriptions.

A Packed Listing Calendar

The week kicks off on August 3 with Propshop Events and Exhibitions and Advance Technoforge making their SME debuts. On August 4, Poojaa Precision Engineering — whose IPO attracted a staggering 259 times oversubscription — joins the boards. The following day, all eyes will be on Manipal Health Enterprises, the Temasek-backed hospital chain whose ₹9,275 crore offering was India's second-largest IPO of 2026 after SBI Funds Management.

"While Manipal Health has a strong pan-India hospital network, leadership in key markets and favorable long-term industry prospects, the rich valuation already factors in much of its growth potential."

— Angel One, in a research note

Manipal Health, which operates over 13,000 beds across 49 hospitals, closed its subscription at 5.12 times, with qualified institutional buyers bidding 8.25 times their allotted portion. Retail participation, however, was more cautious — the retail tranche was subscribed just 0.93 times — as the company's 84.65x earnings valuation came at a premium to listed peers Apollo Hospitals, Max Healthcare, and Fortis Healthcare, which trade between 66x and 75x.

Also listing on August 5 is H.R. Hygiene Products, subscribed 6.26 times. Mainboard entrants MV Electrosystems (8.32x subscribed) and Juniper Green Energy hit the boards on August 6, alongside SME debutants Oneindig Technologies and Dhaval Packaging. Fusion Klassroom Edutech and G.V. Electricals round out the week with August 7 listings.

New IPOs Open for Bidding

Even as listings dominate the first half of the week, fresh issues are queuing up. Anawil Wire & Engineering, an NSE SME offering priced at ₹257–270, opens on August 3 with a ₹178 crore issue size. Aegeus Technologies follows on August 4 with a ₹24 crore BSE SME offering at ₹100–105 per share.

The marquee new opening is Ardee Industries, a mainboard IPO worth ₹426 crore priced at ₹50–53 per share, set for August 5–7. Further out, LAPL Automotive (₹32 crore, ₹88–94) and Technocraft Ventures open later in the week, extending the action through mid-August.

July's Momentum Carries Forward

The August rush follows a stellar July that saw several high-profile listings. Indo-MIM, the precision engineering firm, delivered the month's biggest fireworks with a 44.3% listing pop, debuting at ₹700 against its IPO price of ₹485 after attracting 51.89 times oversubscription. Lohia Corp gained 8.5% on listing day, while Xtranet Technologies added 7.1%.

"The IPO market is showing clear signs of revival, and the next two months should see a meaningful pickup in primary issuances."

— Anirudh Garg, Partner, INVasset PMS

The broader pipeline remains formidable. According to data from Equirus Capital, 236 mainboard draft IPO papers were pending with SEBI as of May 2026, with analysts estimating a ₹60,000 crore fundraising surge between July and September. A looming September 30 SEBI deadline — after which approvals lapse — is pushing many companies to accelerate their timelines.

What It Means for NRI Investors

For the Indian diaspora watching markets from abroad, the current IPO cycle offers both opportunity and caution. NRIs can participate in Indian IPOs through their NRE or NRO demat accounts, and the pipeline includes sectors ranging from healthcare and green energy to precision manufacturing. However, fund managers are urging discipline.

"Considering the large issue size and valuations that already reflect much of the positive outlook, we are expecting a muted listing," said Prasenjit Paul, fund manager at Kolkata-based 129 Wealth, referring to Manipal Health, according to Reuters.

What's Next

The marquee names are still ahead. Adtech unicorn InMobi is preparing a $1 billion IPO at an expected $8–10 billion valuation, having recently appointed JPMorgan Chase, Jefferies, Kotak Mahindra Capital, and Axis Capital as bankers. Travel platform MakeMyTrip has filed confidentially with SEBI for a $1 billion OFS-only IPO of its India subsidiary. And the biggest of all — the National Stock Exchange — is expected to file its preliminary papers imminently, a listing that could redefine India's capital markets landscape.
nri_angle: NRI investors can participate in India's current IPO boom through NRE/NRO demat accounts, with opportunities spanning healthcare, green energy, and precision manufacturing sectors.
